rationale: The answer turns on what happens when the reveal is impossible: 701.44a states the explore process and its 'Otherwise, that player puts a +1/+1 counter on the exploring permanent' branch, which is exactly the outcome given. The not-losing-the-game half is already covered by 104.3c.
answer_excerpt: Alvaro can't reveal the top card of their library, so they put a +1/+1 counter on the Merfolk Branchwalker.

rationale: The answer's load-bearing claim is that protection did not save Goblin Outlander from a non-targeting white spell (Day of Judgment). 702.16b is the only protection rule governing spells, and it limits that protection to being targeted, so a spell that destroys without targeting is unaffected. No rule states 'protection doesn't prevent destruction' positively; 702.16b is the rule that would have applied and doesn't.
answer_excerpt: Protection does not prevent a permanent from being destroyed, so Goblin Outlander dies.

rationale: The parent stands in for the transform action itself: 701.27a states that transforming is turning the permanent over so its other face is up and that only permanents represented by double-faced cards/tokens can do it, which is why the copy-of-a-DFC Convicted Killer can transform at all. The copy-face consequences are already carried by 707.2b, 707.8 and 712.18.
answer_excerpt: Both Duskwatch Recruiter and Convicted Killer transform.

rationale: Same point as rg134 but via an ability: Teysa's triggered ability destroys without targeting. 702.16b is the only protection rule about abilities, limiting protection to 'can't be targeted by abilities from a source with the stated quality', so a non-targeting destroy ability from a black source still works.
answer_excerpt: The protection granted by Black Ward doesn't prevent destruction.

rationale: The answer turns on the fight itself dealing the damage that Dralnu then replaces, killing Golden Guardian mid-resolution. 701.14a states that each creature instructed to fight deals damage equal to its power to the other creature. The ordering and delayed-trigger points are already carried by 608.2c and 603.7a.
answer_excerpt: Golden Guardian dies as the fight occurs.

rationale: The answer's decisive sentence is that creating the tokens and their entering the battlefield are the same event, so a creation-modifying effect (Doubling Season) and an ETB-modifying effect (Gather Specimens) both apply to it. 701.7a states that creating tokens IS putting them onto the battlefield, which is what makes them one event. 701.7b was considered and rejected: it governs ordering relative to continuous effects that modify characteristics, not the same-event identity the answer rests on.
answer_excerpt: It doesn't matter that Doubling Season applies to the creation of the tokens while Gather Specimens applies to them entering the battlefield- it's still the same event.

rationale: Same same-event point as rg525: Crafty Cutpurse modifies token creation while Gather Specimens modifies entering the battlefield, and the answer rests on those being one event. 701.7a equates creating tokens with putting them onto the battlefield. Replacement-effect sequencing is already carried by 614.5 and 616.2.
answer_excerpt: It doesn't matter that Crafty Cutpurse applies to the creation of the tokens while Crafty Cutpurse applies to them entering the battlefield- it's still the same event.

rationale: 701.27e is already in gold and covers the 'transforms into' trigger. The parent was standing in for the base transform action, stated by 701.27a (turn it over so its other face is up; only double-faced permanents can transform), which is why the copy Instigator Gang transforms at all.

The answer turns on splice being paid as an additional cost while the spell is cast, before it resolves and produces mana. 702.47a states verbatim that you reveal the card 'as you cast' the spell and 'pay [cost] as an additional cost to cast that spell'.
answer_excerpt: Ashley chooses whether they are splicing anything onto Desperate Ritual and then pays its cost as Desperate Ritual is cast.

rationale: The whole answer is that Bloodline Pretender's changeling makes it every creature type, hence a Sand and a Warrior. 702.73a states that changeling means 'This object is every creature type.' It is also the parent's only child.
answer_excerpt: Yes. It's a Sand and a Warrior.
